cards.task: Use the key to open the door, then reach the goal.

wrong.why: Takes the key and opens the door, then never reaches the goal.

cards.notes: Task text: first task of examples/arm-fm/minigrid-doorkey/tasks.json. Pilot bundle generated from this text. Changed in card fix 2: the key-before-door and door-before-goal orders are forced by the world, so they are optional extras in scoring (`forced`); Existence(at_goal) alone is also a correct output. S2 2026-11-19: the Response chain with the first trigger required (Response(first, door_open), Response(door_open, last), Existence(first)) is also a correct output (`also_ok`), the same alternative the pilot and smoke copies of this card already carry. Order audit 2026-11-20: the task states both orders ("use the key to open the door", "then reach the goal"), and a stated order is required even when the level forces it, so `forced` is gone and Existence(at_goal) alone is no longer correct. The Response chain stays `also_ok`: it states both orders as "after a, b". Card fixes 2026-11-20: the Response chain left `also_ok` too. `Response` is not a step form, so it does not carry the stated orders (user rule); the pilot and smoke copies lost it the same day.

cards.task: Acquire the matching key, unlock the door, and pick up the designated box in the other room.

wrong.why: Takes the key and opens the door, then never picks up the box.

cards.notes: Task text: first task of examples/arm-fm/minigrid-unlock-pickup/tasks.json. Pilot bundle generated from this text. The agent carries one object, so it drops the key before taking the box. Changed in card fix 2: the key-before-door and door-before-box orders are forced by the world, so they are optional extras in scoring (`forced`); Existence(target_picked_up) alone is also a correct output. S2 2026-11-19: the Response chain with the first trigger required (Response(first, door_open), Response(door_open, last), Existence(first)) is also a correct output (`also_ok`), the same alternative the pilot and smoke copies of this card already carry. Order audit 2026-11-20: both orders stay `forced`. The task lists the steps with no order word ("Acquire ..., unlock ..., and pick up ..."), so it states no order; the same reading makes "Open the door and pick up the box" two goals. This is the closest call of the audit; the pilot and smoke copies of this card require both orders. Stated-order rule 2026-11-20 (user): only order words ("then", "after", "before") give an order, so this plain list is three facts. `expect` is one Existence per fact, the ordered chain (the old `expect`) is the `also_ok` answer, and `forced` is gone. The Response chain left `also_ok`: it is neither the facts nor the chain, and `Response` is not a step form (the base-doorkey ruling). The chain with all three Existences is also accepted (second `also_ok`): it equals the chain; the extra Existences are implied (MONA: same LTLf; same states and transitions, only the hard-break and end charges grow). Order rule 2026-11-21 (user): commanded steps in one sentence, joined by commas or "and", keep their written order, so the list states key before door before box. `expect` gains both `Precedence` clauses at its end (the plans' `breaks` stay valid; the world forces both orders), the chain stays `also_ok`, and the chain with all three Existences left `also_ok`, since it is now `expect`.

cards.task: Pick up the blocking ball and the key, in either order, unlock the door, and then pick up the box in the other room.

wrong.why: Clears the ball, takes the key and opens the door, then never picks up the box.

cards.notes: Task text: first task of examples/arm-fm/minigrid-blocked-unlock-pickup/tasks.json. The first drop must leave the door reachable. Changed in card fix 2: the wording now says the ball and the key may come in either order (the example task text keeps the ball-first list), because a key-first run satisfies every clause; the three orders are forced by the world, so they are optional extras in scoring (`forced`) and Existence(target_picked_up) alone is also a correct output. Order audit 2026-11-20: the list "..., unlock the door, and then pick up the box" states all three orders (the ball and the key before the door, the door before the box), and a stated order is required even when the level forces it, so `forced` is gone and Existence(target_picked_up) alone is no longer correct.

cards.task: Explore the side rooms, find and acquire the key matching the locked target room, return to the corridor, open the target door, and pick up the designated object.

wrong.why: Takes the key and opens the target door, then never picks up the object.

cards.notes: Task text: first task of examples/arm-fm/minigrid-key-corridor/tasks.json. Navigation opens closed unlocked side doors on the way. Changed in card fix 2: the key-before-door and door-before-object orders are forced by the world, so they are optional extras in scoring (`forced`); Existence(target_picked_up) alone is also a correct output, and the card does not measure exploration. Order audit 2026-11-20: both orders stay `forced`. The task lists the steps with no order word, so it states no order (the same reading as base-unlock-pickup). The stated "find and acquire the key" has no clause in `expect`; listed for review. Card fixes 2026-11-20: no change. "Find and acquire the key" is the key step, and `expect` names it (`has_matching_key`, in the first `Precedence`); `key_found` would add nothing, since the facts page says the key is never held before it is seen; "explore the side rooms" and "return to the corridor" have no label. Moved from KeyCorridorS6R3 to KeyCorridorS4R3 on 2026-11-20 (with cx-sequence): no method learned S6R3 in 71 runs. `expect` and the answer lists are unchanged. The S4R3 FARM bundle (production pair, `--reasoning max`, end judgment off: the default `reward_end_judgment`) adds Precedence(key_found, has_matching_key) beyond the card. That is on the LLM side: it read "find and acquire" as an order, and the user's rule is that only order words such as "then", "after" and "before" give an order. The scorer calls the clauses `mismatch`, so its training on S4R3 (FARM 2 of 3 seeds, no-RM 0 of 3) is kept as a probe only, not a benchmark result. The bundle is generated again after the card is updated for the user's stated-order rule. ARM-FM, 2026-11-20: the ARM-FM bundle still has the S6R3 page and room geometry; `run-suite` refuses it (bundle level mismatch), and it is generated again at the freeze. Stated-order rule 2026-11-20 (user): the plain list gives facts, but the compound "find and acquire the key" states an order (taking the key needs finding it first; user: "this one is fine"), so `expect` is Precedence(key_found, has_matching_key) with one Existence per fact, the ordered chain with that Precedence is the only `also_ok` answer, `forced` is gone, and the S4R3 FARM bundle above is correct and not generated again: its training counts (FARM 2 of 3 seeds, judged success 0.85, 0.82, 0.00 at 1.5M steps; no-RM 0 of 3). Order rule 2026-11-21 (user): commanded steps in one sentence, joined by commas or "and", keep their written order, so the list also states key before door before object. `expect` gains Precedence(has_matching_key, target_door_open) and Precedence(target_door_open, target_picked_up) at its end (the plans' `breaks` stay valid); the 4-clause chain stays `also_ok` and now states the same task as `expect`. The S4R3 FARM bundle above stores exactly that chain, so it stays right (`also_ok`).

cards.task: Explore the side rooms, find and acquire the key matching the locked target room, return to the corridor, open the target door, and pick up the designated object.

wrong.why: Takes the key and opens the target door, then never picks up the object.

cards.notes: World-size copy of base-key-corridor for the difficulty test (user, 2026-11-22): the same task, `expect`, answer lists and plans in a KeyCorridorS3R3 world (room_size 3, 7x7 grid), trained on the base-key-corridor FARM bundle (`bundle_of`; no paraphrases and no bundle of its own, so generate-suite skips it). The gym id stays KeyCorridorS4R3 with `room_size` in `env_kwargs`: run-suite refuses a borrowed bundle whose environment page does not name the card's gym id (bundle level mismatch), and that page names only S4R3 and S6R3. `max_steps` is 480, the S4R3 limit (the S3R3 limit is 270), because the machine is priced for 480 steps and train-rl's pay check refuses another limit. `train` is false: the card is not in the counted 60-card set; the difficulty test's own runs file trains it. Check 2026-11-22 (`experiments/benchmark/envs/minigrid-key-corridor/check/size_copy_check.py`, on the judge's 100 reset seeds): the pay check accepts the bundle; the plan checker passes (the solving plan ends final, the wrong and idle plans stay open to the step limit). The side rooms are one cell, so on 60 seeds the planner finds no safe cell to drop the key; there the solving plan with a free drop ends final too, so the solve ends final on all 100 seeds within 35 steps (median 19 where the planner runs, 23 with the free drop). The bundle's labeling equals the reference labeler on every step of the plan traces and of 100 random walks to the step limit.
